headlineChange: KADOMA still opens maximised and on top, but it now steps aside when another window needs to be used: a mail compose window, the printer driver's preferences dialog, a file shown in Explorer, and Windows Settings can all come to the front. The topmost style is restored when the person returns to KADOMA. The unlimited-combine behaviour from 0.28.1 is unchanged.

validation.windowFrontRoutesVerified: tests/test_window_front.py asserts /api/share/email, /api/share/reveal, /api/system/print/preferences and the default-app Settings action each call yield_front() before handing off, that an overlong email is refused without yielding, and that clipboard/prepare do not yield at all.

defectsFoundAndFixedThisRelease: WS_EX_TOPMOST is unconditional, so a mail compose window or the printer driver's settings dialog appeared behind KADOMA and could not be used. A new app/window_front.py drops the style before a hand-off and a watcher restores it when KADOMA is active again. Four server routes now call yield_front() first: share/email, share/reveal, system/print/preferences and the default-app Settings action.

Toggling topmost through pywebview's public window.on_top setter would have to run on the WebView2 UI thread, but the hand-off arrives on the server thread. The implementation uses SetWindowPos through ctypes instead, which the window manager marshals — proven by a real window driven from a background thread.

A release asked for before the window existed, or one whose SetWindowPos failed, used to be dropped silently. FrontGuard now keeps the request and the watcher applies it as soon as the HWND is available.

An external window that never takes focus could have left KADOMA permanently demoted. An 8-second fallback restores the style, but only when no other window has actually been seen in front — a compose window kept open for as long as needed is never interrupted.
measuredLimitations: The topmost hand-off is Windows-only. app/window_front.py is a pure-ctypes no-op on macOS and Linux; those builds keep pywebview's on_top flag unchanged, so the same covering behaviour could occur there.

The actual Outlook compose window and the real printer driver dialog were not opened from the shipped 0.28.2 EXE. scripts/check_window_front.py reproduces the situation with a separate process's window and asserts the Z-order reversal; the four routes are asserted to call yield_front() before handing off.

An external window that never takes the foreground is covered by an 8-second fallback that restores the style. Once another window has been seen in front, no timeout applies — KADOMA stays demoted until the person comes back to it.

The right-click entry was verified by reading the registry back and by running the exact command Explorer runs. The menu itself was not clicked in Explorer, so Windows' expansion of %* for a multi-selection is taken from its documented behaviour rather than observed here.

'Unlimited' means no application-imposed file count. The Explorer verb still passes the selection as one command line, so Windows' CreateProcess ceiling (~32,767 characters) is the physical wall: roughly 100-120 files with long paths, more with short names. Exceeding it is an operating-system limit, not a KADOMA refusal. Truly removing it needs a COM DropTarget shell extension, which was not built.

Combining 25 files was verified through the server endpoint and the engine, not by clicking the Explorer menu with 25 files selected. The menu's behaviour at that count is inferred from the verb definition and the endpoint test, not observed in Explorer.
The menu entry is written at every start, for the current user only. A machine policy that blocks HKCU\Software\Classes makes the entry fail silently; the application still works.
Combining from Explorer reads the files from disk, so it is desktop-only. A browser preview has no such route, and the endpoint answers 403 there.
Dark is the default, but a stored light choice wins. Anybody who had already switched to light keeps it — the default only decides what a fresh profile sees.

Acrobat itself was not driven. It is installed here but closes on start in its trial state, so the application the /DR and /P work is aimed at could not be observed opening the file. The structure those keys require is asserted, and a second engine fills the same file.
Chrome tolerated the missing /DR before this release as well, so check_reader.py is a regression guard rather than proof that the fix was needed for Chrome.
The compose route depends on a mail client with a command line: Outlook or Thunderbird. A machine with only a Store mail app falls back to the .eml, and the note says so.

On top is not absolute any more: a mail compose window, printer preferences, Explorer and Windows Settings ask the shell to drop WS_EX_TOPMOST first, and the style returns when KADOMA is the active window again. Clicking an unrelated window that KADOMA did not open does not trigger this — the application stays on top in that case.

Two-sided printing could not be exercised end to end on this machine: every printer installed is a virtual one that reports no duplex support, so the control is correctly shown disabled. The setting path is covered by tests; paper coming out on both sides is not.
Acrobat itself was not run. The date actions are the ones Acrobat writes and the PDF structure is asserted, but "Acrobat shows its picker" is an expectation, not an observation here.

Prepare Form is rule-based: it finds underscore rules, drawn boxes and Label: lines. It does not understand a table-shaped form with no rules, and it can offer a field where a line was a separator — which is why every candidate is listed and can be unticked first.
500 MB is a limit, not a promise about memory: a 500 MB document is held in memory while open, and undo is capped separately at 100 MB of snapshots.

Paper size and orientation are Windows-only: they go through the driver's DEVMODE. On macOS and Linux the two controls are shown disabled and the dialog says the printer does not report its paper sizes, rather than pretending.
The paper and orientation belong to the driver for the session. Changing them for one job leaves the printer set that way, exactly as changing them in the driver's own dialog would.
Duplex, quality, tray and colour are not in the print dialog. They stay in Printer properties, because they differ per driver and the driver can describe them.
150% is a size, not a fit: a very large page at 150% needs horizontal scrolling, and Fit width is one press away.
The email is still not sent by KADOMA. The draft is handed to the mail program and nothing leaves the machine until somebody presses Send.
The copy dialog chooses the file name, not the location: where it goes is the desktop Save dialog's business, and the browser preview puts it wherever downloads go.
The page copy is one page at a time. Two or more pages is the export dialog, which already has a page range.
The tool list is not configurable: it shows every tool in the same order as Home, and cannot be reordered or trimmed.
Which panels are showing, including the tool list, lasts for the session. It is not remembered after the application closes.
The comparison is of words, not of pixels. A moved paragraph reads as removed and added, and images, drawings and layout are not compared.
Resizing scales uniformly — the smaller of the two factors — so a change of aspect ratio leaves a margin rather than stretching the content.
A stamp does not avoid collisions: it is drawn where it is clicked, which can be on top of existing text.
Links are web addresses and page jumps only. No JavaScript actions, no links to other files, and a link's rectangle cannot be edited after it is made.

The stamps are drawn marks, not Acrobat's standard stamp annotations: they carry the right words and colour and are real text, but a reader that lists stamps by their standard name will not find them under one.

The four new tools are tested against the engine and driven through the interface, but the frozen build's self-test does not exercise them individually — it proves the module is bundled by starting the application, which imports it.

The seven new tools are tested against the engine and driven through the interface, but the frozen build's self-test does not exercise them individually — it proves the module is bundled by starting the application, which imports it.
Compression is only as good as the images in the file: a text-only PDF shrinks a few per cent, a scan-heavy one can halve. The dialog reports the result rather than promising a figure.
Bookmark generation reads type sizes. A document with no size hierarchy produces a short outline or none, not a guess per line.

The dirty close is verified in two halves — the page decision and dialog in a browser, and pywebview's cancel-then-ask mechanism in a probe window — not as one end-to-end run: a native window's UI cannot be scripted here, so nobody has clicked "Save and close" on the real window.
The browser preview still shows the browser's own "leave site?" prompt when there are unsaved changes. That dialog is the browser's, and it only appears when there is something to lose.
Closing takes about 2.7 s while the local service shuts down; that is teardown, not a dialog.
Editing a scan by dragging destroys what is underneath: the pixels are removed and painted over. It replaces a box, not a reflowed paragraph.
OCR still needs Tesseract installed, replaces the page with a 200-DPI raster, and does not report a confidence figure.
The Date tool places the date exactly where it is clicked, so it can land on top of existing text; it does not avoid collisions.
Making a scan editable needs Tesseract installed locally. Without it the button routes to the OCR panel and its install instructions rather than failing silently.

OCR replaces the page with a searchable 200-DPI raster: annotations on that page are flattened and form fields on it are removed. The confirmation says so first. Recognition quality depends on the scan and the tool does not report a confidence figure.

The reported print hang could not be reproduced here: eight sheets to a real printer driver took 0.9 s. A three-minute deadline and a sheet count in the overlay now make a genuine hang visible instead of leaving an overlay that never clears, but the underlying cause is in the printer driver and was not observed.
Closing the whole window relies on the browser beforeunload prompt; the desktop shell may not show it. The tested path is closing a document tab.
The editor now renders every page, but only pages near the viewport are fetched — a very long document scrolled quickly will briefly show blank sheets while they arrive.
Collated and uncollated are verified as the order of sheets handed to the spooler, not as the order that comes out of a physical tray, because no physical printer was used.

The order is built by the application and sent as a list of sheets rather than set on the driver, so it does not depend on a driver collate setting — but it also means the driver is not the thing collating.

The printer-properties dialog has not been opened by a human. The DEVMODE round-trip behind it is tested without prompting, and the button is wired to the endpoint, but nobody has clicked OK in a real driver dialog.
No physical printer was used. Every job went to a driver that writes a file.
Copies are drawn as repeated pages inside one job rather than set on the driver, so they come out collated (1, 2, 3, then 1, 2, 3).
Duplex, paper size and scaling are not offered in the application's own dialog; they live in the printer driver's settings, which the dialog opens.
There is no page range in the export path beyond what already existed; printing has one.
The Pages view is a scrolling grid of page cards, not a continuous single-column document view. The editor still shows one page at a time.
The home screen is a map of actions, not a document browser: Recent lists the documents open in this workspace, held in memory for the session.
Two cards that Acrobat shows are deliberately absent: Request e-signatures and Send for Comments.
The supplied artwork is a 1080 px JPEG, so the 1024 px PNG and the 256 px ICO are resampled from it.
The source folder is still named `paperdesk` on disk and inside the source archive (`kadoma-pdf/` for the kit).
Save writes over the file you opened, with no version history, no automatic backup and no undo after a save. Save as is the way to keep the original.
A file that changed on disk since it was opened cannot be saved over at all. The way forward is Save as.
Saving is a desktop feature. The browser preview has nowhere to write, says so, and offers the export instead.
A document opened from the browser's file picker, created blank, or converted from Word or Excel has no file behind it, so its first Save asks for a destination.

The two native file dialogs need a human to operate them. The contract around them is tested, and the save path is driven end to end against a real file, but the dialogs themselves are not exercised by any automated check.
The only thing stored on the machine is the light/dark choice, in one localStorage key.
The window arrangement is not remembered. Which panels are open, and how far the page is zoomed, last for the session only.
The page is not rendered above 3.2x, so a page zoomed to 300% on a high-density display is resampled rather than rendered at full device resolution.
The offline reading is not a language model. It selects sentences already in the document and quotes them; it does not paraphrase, translate, summarise in its own words, or answer questions.
No question answering, chat, translation, rewriting or document generation.
A connected model is not verified for truth. Whatever it returns is validated for shape but not for accuracy, and no real provider was used to verify this release.
Only the extracted text is sent to a model, never the file, and never the document's images, annotations or form values.
No key is stored. Closing the application forgets the connection, and the key is never written to disk, logged, or returned by any endpoint.
There are no tabs, no split view and no side-by-side comparison. One document is on screen at a time.
Documents are edited in memory and written only on request, so quitting loses anything not saved or exported.
The workspace holds six documents. Opening more closes the oldest without asking.
A protected PDF cannot be split, and a PDF whose owner forbids page assembly cannot be merged or split.
Splitting divides by page count, not by file size, so a document with mixed page sizes produces parts of uneven size.
Combining does not shrink the result: pages are copied as they are and the output is not re-compressed.
A PDF has no date field type, so a KADOMA PDF date field is a text field carrying two private keys.
Clearing a form clears the whole document rather than the current page. Read-only fields are deliberately skipped.
Arabic-Indic digits may return in the equivalent Extended/Persian variant; search folds the variants, but extracted text is not byte-identical to the input.
The bundled Noto Sans Arabic fallback font is approximate: it renders correctly but does not round-trip the lam-alef ligature exactly.
Font round-trip quality is measured per machine. On Windows, Arial and Tahoma are exact; Segoe UI, Dubai, Microsoft Sans Serif and Calibri lose the lam-alef ligature.
The Windows default-app flow ends in a Settings page the user must confirm.
The double-click handoff is much slower for the one-file build than for the portable folder build.
hostedPreviewProcessing: Remote hosted workspace; non-sensitive samples only. Sharing, printing, default-app and saving refuse the request in this mode rather than pretending to work; the interface explains that they need the desktop app. The AI reading works in the preview too, and the model connection sends the document's text from the hosted workspace rather than from the visitor's computer.
optionalEngines: an OpenAI-compatible model endpoint (optional, off by default, the user's own)
